heuristics.rule: Winter graduates get one extra H-1B lottery attempt compared to spring graduates
heuristics.condition: When timing your graduation as an international student pursuing H-1B
heuristics.action: If possible, arrange to graduate in December/winter rather than spring, to gain an extra advanced-degree lottery draw
heuristics.because: The post explains that winter graduates can participate in 3 advanced-degree draws while spring graduates only get 2 advanced-degree draws plus 1 regular draw, improving cumulative odds to roughly 80%

heuristics.rule: Begin OPT EAD application no later than 120 days before graduation
heuristics.condition: When approaching graduation date on F-1 status
heuristics.action: Submit OPT EAD application within the 120-day window before graduation
heuristics.because: The post explicitly states the application window opens 120 days before graduation and processing time must be factored in to avoid gaps

heuristics.rule: Start H-1B petition materials preparation at least 2 months before April 1 filing window
heuristics.condition: When planning to file H-1B in the upcoming cap season
heuristics.action: Begin collecting and preparing petition materials in January–February to be ready for the April 1 window
heuristics.because: The post notes that despite the official April 1 filing date, practical preparation requires starting approximately 2 months earlier

heuristics.rule: After I-140 approval, job changes require a new PERM but the original priority date can be preserved
heuristics.condition: When changing employers while in the EB-2 green card queue
heuristics.action: Transfer H-1B and restart PERM at the new employer, then link the new I-140 to the original priority date
heuristics.because: The post explicitly explains that a new PERM is required when changing jobs but the earlier PD can be ported, so the queue position is not lost

heuristics.rule: Once H-1B reaches the 6-year cap, it can be extended indefinitely if an approved I-140 is on file
heuristics.condition: When approaching the H-1B 6-year maximum while waiting in the EB-2 backlog
heuristics.action: Ensure I-140 is approved before H-1B hits 6 years to qualify for annual extensions beyond the cap
heuristics.because: The post states this as a key benefit of being in the EB queue: 'H1B满6年后可以无限续期'

decision_factors.factor: Country of birth (mainland China vs. other)
decision_factors.why_it_matters: EB-2 applicants born in mainland China face a per-country cap of 7% of total EB visas, creating backlogs of many years, while applicants from most other countries face no meaningful wait
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check the USCIS Visa Bulletin for the current EB-2 China priority date and compare it to when you expect to file PERM

decision_factors.why_it_matters: PhD holders can pursue EB-1B (outstanding researcher) or EB-1A routes which historically had no China backlog; MS holders are effectively limited to EB-2 or EB-3, which have severe China backlogs
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Assess your research publication record and whether you have realistic prospects for EB-1 qualification before committing to a green card strategy

decision_factors.factor: H-1B lottery outcome timing relative to OPT expiration
decision_factors.why_it_matters: If OPT expires before H-1B is approved, the person loses work authorization and must find alternative status or leave; managing this gap is critical
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Calculate OPT end date including STEM extension, map it against potential H-1B effective dates (October 1 each year), and identify how many lottery cycles fit within the OPT window

decision_factors.factor: Employer willingness to sponsor and initiate PERM quickly
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The earlier the PERM is filed, the earlier the priority date, which determines queue position in the China EB-2 backlog — delays of even one year can matter significantly
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask prospective employers explicitly about their green card sponsorship timeline policy and whether they initiate after 1 year of employment

decision_factors.factor: Marital status and spouse's immigration status
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Marrying a US citizen provides the fastest path to a green card (2 years vs. 10+ years for EB-2 China); marrying a green card holder still requires several years of wait but bypasses the EB queue entirely
decision_factors.how_to_assess: The post explicitly ranks marriage-based green card paths by sponsor status: I-485 pending holder > citizen > non-Chinese/non-Indian student > green card holder > H-1B with I-140

decision_factors.factor: Current EB-2 China priority date vs. expected PERM filing date
decision_factors.why_it_matters: The backlog was already at 6+ years as of 2016 and worsening; someone filing PERM today may face 10–15+ years of waiting
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Monitor the monthly Visa Bulletin; calculate expected PERM filing date and compare to current cutoff date to estimate wait time

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Staying in H-1B status while waiting for EB-2 green card approval
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: H-1B status is immediately voided if you lose your job, regardless of where you are in the green card queue — years of queue position can be rendered instantly useless by a layoff
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Anyone deep in the EB-2 China backlog (5+ years in) who gets laid off and cannot quickly find a new sponsoring employer

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Changing employers while in the EB-2 green card queue
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Requires restarting the entire PERM process (9–12 months) at the new employer, meaning a period of no active green card petition and potential status vulnerability
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: People who receive better job offers mid-queue and do not realize the priority date portability benefit requires a new I-140 to be filed and approved first

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Pursuing MS (employment-oriented) instead of PhD for faster entry into the workforce
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: MS holders are effectively locked out of EB-1A/EB-1B routes, which have historically had much shorter or no China backlogs — committing to EB-2 means accepting a potentially 10+ year wait
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Mainland China-born MS graduates in CS who prioritize speed to employment but do not account for the downstream green card bottleneck

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Relying on STEM OPT extension for multiple H-1B lottery attempts
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The 29-month OPT window creates a false sense of security — if H-1B is not secured within that window, the person must switch to a non-work status, leave, or pursue marriage/asylum routes
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: Students who assume that multiple lottery chances make H-1B nearly certain, without planning for the scenario where all attempts fail

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Marrying a green card holder for immigration purposes
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Spouse in F-2 status cannot work and cannot use F-1 CPT/OPT because F-2 demonstrates immigrant intent; they must independently obtain H/L/O visa status to work during the multi-year F2A wait
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students who marry green card holders expecting to maintain work authorization during the green card process

failure_patterns.pattern: Underestimating the EB-2 China backlog length when making the decision to pursue a US green card via MS+employment
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: The backlog is invisible at the time of the MS application decision; students focus on the achievable near-term goal (get a job, get H-1B) without modeling the 10-year downstream timeline
failure_patterns.consequence: A person completes MS, gets sponsored for H-1B, files PERM, and then realizes they face a 10+ year wait for a green card — often during prime career and family formation years
warning_signs: Assuming the process ends at H-1B approval
Not checking the current EB-2 China priority date before committing to the MS+employment path

failure_patterns.pattern: Letting OPT expire without securing H-1B or an alternative status
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Students assume H-1B odds are high enough that planning for failure is unnecessary; each failed lottery reduces available OPT time until options run out
failure_patterns.consequence: Loss of work authorization, forced departure or switch to non-work status (F-1, B-2), career interruption
warning_signs: Not calculating exact OPT expiration date against lottery timelines
No contingency plan for 2 consecutive lottery failures

failure_patterns.pattern: Changing jobs without understanding the PERM restart requirement
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: Employees believe priority date portability means the green card process simply 'transfers' to the new employer, not realizing PERM must be restarted from scratch
failure_patterns.consequence: Gap in active green card petition, potential loss of I-140 if not approved before switching, delayed green card timeline
warning_signs: Accepting a new job offer without consulting an immigration attorney first
Assuming the new employer's HR will handle the transfer automatically

diagnostic_questions.question: What is your country of birth?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines whether EB per-country caps create a multi-decade backlog (mainland China, India) or whether EB-2 is realistically achievable within a few years
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If mainland China: ask what year you expect to file PERM and compare to the current EB-2 China cutoff date to estimate your wait
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If not China/India: EB-2 backlog is minimal; focus on H-1B lottery strategy and PERM timing instead

diagnostic_questions.question: Are you pursuing a PhD or an MS?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: PhD opens EB-1A/EB-1B routes which bypass or significantly reduce the China per-country backlog; MS effectively limits you to EB-2 or EB-3
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If PhD: assess your publication record and likelihood of qualifying for EB-1B (outstanding researcher) as a faster path
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If MS: plan for EB-2 with a realistic 10-year timeline and evaluate whether the US green card is the right long-term goal

diagnostic_questions.question: When does your OPT (including STEM extension) expire, and how many H-1B lottery cycles does that allow?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Determines the maximum number of H-1B attempts available before losing work authorization, and whether there is a contingency plan if all attempts fail
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If 2+ lottery cycles remain: calculate cumulative probability of at least one success and plan contingency for all-failure scenario
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If only 1 cycle remains: the risk of OPT expiration without H-1B is significant; identify fallback options now (cap-exempt employers, Canada, marriage, return home)

diagnostic_questions.question: Has your employer indicated when they will initiate the PERM process after you join?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: The PERM filing date becomes your priority date — every month of delay in starting the process is a month added to the end of a 10+ year wait for China-born applicants
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: If employer initiates within 1 year: proceed and verify the PERM is filed as early as possible
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: If employer has no clear policy or delays beyond 2 years: the priority date disadvantage compounds the already-long backlog

industry_realities.common_belief: Getting a CS MS degree from the US and landing a job means you're on a clear path to a green card
industry_realities.actual_reality: For mainland China-born applicants, the EB-2 backlog means the realistic timeline from MS graduation to green card is approximately 10 years, and the situation was actively worsening as of 2016 — EB-1 for India/China began backing up, eliminating spillover quota relief for EB-2 China
industry_realities.implication: Students should treat the green card as a 10-year project requiring sustained employment stability, not an expected outcome of getting a good job

industry_realities.common_belief: H-1B advanced degree lottery gives MS graduates a high chance of approval
industry_realities.actual_reality: As of 2015, with 233,000 applicants, the advanced degree lottery success rate was approximately 60% per attempt — and the post notes this rate was declining as applicant numbers grew year over year
industry_realities.implication: Do not treat H-1B as a near-certain outcome; plan for the possibility of 2 failed lotteries and have a concrete backup plan before OPT expires

industry_realities.common_belief: STEM OPT extension gives you 29 months, so you have plenty of time to secure H-1B
industry_realities.actual_reality: 29 months allows 2–3 lottery attempts but each failure leaves less runway; if H-1B is not secured within OPT, the only remaining legal options are marriage-based green card, asylum, cap-exempt employers, or departure
industry_realities.implication: Treat the 29-month clock as a hard deadline and plan backwards from it, not as a comfortable buffer

industry_realities.common_belief: Changing jobs while waiting for a green card is straightforward since you can port your priority date
industry_realities.actual_reality: Priority date portability requires the original I-140 to have been approved; changing jobs means restarting the entire PERM process (9–12 months) at the new employer, during which there is no active green card petition protecting you
industry_realities.implication: Job changes during the green card process require immigration attorney consultation and careful timing to avoid resetting the clock unnecessarily

industry_realities.common_belief: School prestige matters a lot for getting a job and visa sponsorship as a CS MS student
industry_realities.actual_reality: The post explicitly states '学校好坏就不重要了' (school quality doesn't matter much) for employment-track MS students in CS — what matters is getting the degree, the internship, and the full-time offer from a sponsoring employer
industry_realities.implication: Spending significantly more money on a higher-ranked program for employment purposes may not improve immigration outcomes

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How they think about the green card timeline
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Thinks of the process as: get MS → get job → get H-1B → get green card, with each step taking 1–2 years
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Maps out the full 10-year sequence explicitly: MS (2yr) + H-1B lottery (1–2yr) + work (0.5–1yr) + PERM (0.5–1yr) + I-140 + EB-2 China queue (4–5yr+) and recognizes the queue is worsening
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Underestimating the timeline leads to life decisions (marriage, housing, family) made on false assumptions about when permanent status will arrive

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Asks only 'will this employer sponsor H-1B?' and considers the answer yes/no
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Asks how quickly the employer initiates PERM after hire, whether they have a track record of filing I-140, and whether they will support priority date portability if you change roles internally
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A 1-year delay in PERM initiation compounds over the backlog period; early priority date is one of the few variables the employee can influence

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How they think about the H-1B lottery
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Calculates single-attempt odds and assumes they will get lucky; does not plan for failure
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Calculates cumulative multi-attempt odds, maps each attempt against the OPT expiration date, and has a concrete contingency plan (cap-exempt employer, Canada, return home) before the first lottery
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Failure to plan for lottery failure can result in sudden loss of work authorization with no fallback

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: How they think about PhD vs. MS for immigration purposes
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Sees PhD as harder and longer with no practical benefit over MS for getting a job
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Recognizes that PhD + strong publication record opens EB-1A/EB-1B routes that largely bypass the China per-country backlog, potentially saving 5–8 years of queue time
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: For mainland China-born applicants, the PhD route may actually be faster to permanent residency despite taking longer to complete

community_misconceptions.misconception: Once you get H-1B and your employer files for a green card, your immigration status is secure even if you lose your job
community_misconceptions.why_believed: People conflate 'being in the green card process' with having protected status; the I-140 approval feels like a milestone that should protect you
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: H-1B status is tied to the sponsoring employer — losing your job immediately invalidates H-1B status regardless of where you are in the green card queue; you have a short grace period but must find new sponsorship quickly
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: A layoff mid-queue can mean losing years of wait time if new employment and H-1B transfer cannot be arranged quickly

community_misconceptions.misconception: The EB-2 green card process takes about 3–5 years total for Chinese applicants
community_misconceptions.why_believed: People hear about the PERM + I-140 + I-485 process taking 1–2 years and do not account for the per-country backlog on top of that
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: As of 2016, the EB-2 China priority date was at January 2010, meaning applicants were waiting 6+ years just in the queue — and the backlog was growing; total process from MS graduation realistically 10 years
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: People commit to the US path expecting to have a green card by their early 30s and instead find themselves still waiting in their late 30s or 40s

community_misconceptions.misconception: OPT can be extended beyond 29 months if Congress passes a proposal to extend it
community_misconceptions.why_believed: Proposals to extend OPT have circulated in policy discussions, creating rumor that extensions are coming
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: As of the post's writing, no proposal to extend OPT beyond 29 months (12 + 17 STEM) had been passed; the 29-month cap should be treated as firm for planning purposes
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Students who delay H-1B planning while waiting for a rumored OPT extension may find themselves out of work authorization with no safety net

community_misconceptions.misconception: School ranking is important for getting a job and H-1B sponsorship as a CS MS student
community_misconceptions.why_believed: School prestige signals quality in academic and some professional contexts; students naturally assume top schools lead to better employment outcomes
community_misconceptions.actual_rule: The post states explicitly that for employment-track MS in CS, school quality does not significantly affect job and sponsorship outcomes — technical skills and internship experience matter more
community_misconceptions.real_consequence: Students overpay for prestigious programs expecting immigration advantages that do not materialize

real_case_outcomes.situation: Mainland China-born student pursues CS MS at a US university with the goal of working and eventually obtaining a green card
real_case_outcomes.decision: Follows the standard path: MS degree (2yr) → OPT → H-1B lottery → EB-2 PERM → I-140 → queue
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Total realistic timeline to green card is approximately 10 years from MS start; as of 2016, EB-2 China backlog was already 6+ years and worsening due to increased PERM filings and loss of spillover quota from EB-1
real_case_outcomes.lesson: The standard MS-to-green-card path for mainland China-born CS graduates is a decade-long process, not a 3–5 year one; anyone entering the path should plan their life (finances, family, career) accordingly

real_case_outcomes.situation: CS PhD student with strong publication record seeking a faster green card path
real_case_outcomes.decision: Pursues postdoc or faculty position (cap-exempt H-1B), applies for EB-1B (outstanding researcher) sponsored by institution
real_case_outcomes.outcome: Fastest possible timeline is 5+ years from PhD start; requires being among the top performers in an already highly selective PhD cohort
real_case_outcomes.lesson: EB-1B is a viable bypass of the China EB-2 backlog but is only accessible to the top fraction of PhD graduates — it requires N publications in top conferences and institutional support, not just completing a PhD

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student asks 'how hard is it to stay and get a green card?' after deciding to pursue a US CS MS
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Confirmation-seeking after a major financial and life commitment has already been made; the decision to apply/enroll is sunk cost, making it psychologically difficult to receive a realistic negative assessment
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Asking the question as if there is a simple encouraging answer; framing it as 'how hard' rather than 'should I plan for this'
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Provide the full quantitative timeline (10 years, worsening backlog, multiple decision points that can derail) before the commitment is made, not after; reframe from 'is it achievable' to 'what is my plan for each failure point'

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student focuses intensely on H-1B lottery odds and probability calculations
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Illusion of control — by calculating odds precisely, the student feels they are managing risk, but the calculation obscures the more important question of what happens if all attempts fail
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Detailed probability math for lottery outcomes with no corresponding plan for the scenario where H-1B is never obtained
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Redirect from probability calculation to contingency planning: 'Assuming you don't get H-1B within your OPT window, what is your Plan B? Have you evaluated cap-exempt employers, Canada, or return home?'

psychological_barriers.trigger: Student discovers the EB-2 China backlog length mid-process (after H-1B is already secured)
psychological_barriers.underlying_state: Escalation of commitment / sunk cost fallacy — having already invested years and resources, the student continues on the same path even when the expected value of the green card has dropped significantly
psychological_barriers.how_it_manifests: Continuing to wait in the EB-2 queue for 10+ years rather than reassessing whether alternative paths (Canada, return home, marriage-based) offer better expected outcomes
psychological_barriers.expert_move: Frame the current queue position as a new decision point, not a commitment: 'Given where you are today, what would you choose if you were starting fresh? The years already invested do not change what is optimal going forward.'

reframing_moves.original_framing: How hard is it to stay and get a green card after a CS MS in the US?
reframing_moves.reframe: The question is not whether it is possible, but whether you are prepared for a 10-year multi-stage process with multiple failure points, each of which requires a different contingency plan
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Shifts the student from a binary achievability question to a project management mindset, making the risks concrete and plannable rather than abstract and frightening
reframing_moves.example_language: 总共耗时2年硕士＋1～2年抽签＋0.5~1年工作＋0.5~1年PERM＋4～5年排期，约10年 (Total time: 2yr MS + 1–2yr lottery + 0.5–1yr work + 0.5–1yr PERM + 4–5yr queue = approximately 10 years)

reframing_moves.original_framing: I need to get H-1B to stay in the US after graduation
reframing_moves.reframe: H-1B is only one of several paths, and for mainland China-born applicants it leads into a decade-long EB-2 queue; marriage-based routes, EB-1 (for PhDs), and Canada are alternatives that may produce permanent status faster
reframing_moves.why_it_works: Breaks the tunnel vision on a single path and surfaces alternative routes the student may not have considered, particularly the marriage-based ranking the post provides
reframing_moves.example_language: 如果题主能通过结婚获得绿卡，就不必为EB2遥遥无期的排期而纠结了 (If you can obtain a green card through marriage, you don't need to worry about the endless EB-2 wait)
